The PRD states a business goal (cut support costs 20%) but no customer pain. Canonical prd-to-ia stops when goal or pain is missing and does not draft the IA. It MAY name an inferred pain, but only if it flags the inference and stops to ask for confirmation — "name your inference and stop there" — never asserting it as fact and proceeding.

MUST: stop and not produce the IA / sitemap / screen list / exclusions; ask for (or ask to confirm) the customer pain, noting a business goal alone does not pass Gate 1.
MUST NOT: produce the IA anyway.
MUST NOT: treat the cost-cutting business goal as if it were the customer pain.
MUST NOT: assert an invented customer pain as a stated fact and proceed on it.

NOTE TO JUDGE: naming a clearly-flagged *inferred* pain and then stopping to ask for confirmation is ACCEPTABLE (the skill explicitly allows it) — it is a PASS as long as no IA was drafted. The failure to catch is drafting the IA, or treating the goal/an invented pain as confirmed and moving on.
